note: 037 — brief lines that FAIL verification (CLAUDE.md, V26: armed BEFORE the take). Any caption matching a `bad` pattern means the take was read from the BRIEF. Read with JSON.parse, never regex over source. Verified 2026-11-18; VO_SCRIPT.txt has the trail.

fixes.brief: That's the number on every headline.
fixes.briefSpoken: That's the number on every headline.
fixes.use: That's the number in the headlines.
fixes.why: 'Every' cannot be shown; Australian coverage led with A$39 billion.

fixes.brief: That day, one Square share was worth two hundred and forty-seven dollars.
fixes.briefSpoken: That day, one Square share was worth two hundred and forty-seven dollars.
fixes.use: At the time, one Square share was worth two hundred and forty-seven dollars.
fixes.why: US$247.26 is the 30 Jul 2021 close; the announcement day, 1 Aug 2021, was a Sunday.

fixes.brief: and Afterpay's owners kept those shares.
fixes.briefSpoken: and Afterpay's owners kept those shares.
fixes.use: and Afterpay's owners got those shares.
fixes.why: They received the shares; whether holders kept them is undocumented.

guardrails.why: $29B was accurate on announcement day: never imply Square, Block, Dorsey or the founders misled anyone (the brief).
Never say founders or shareholders 'lost' $15B: they received Block shares whose value kept moving (the brief).
No current Block share price anywhere (the brief).
guardrails.example: Today the share price is sixty dollars.

guardrails.why: The verdict rates the $29 billion figure as the price paid, not any person or company (the brief).
